India’s Bloom Eyes Southeast Asia and Twice the Rooms After $75 Million Raise

Bloom, a hotel brand in India with a user-oriented tech platform, plans to grow to 12,000 rooms over the next few years and to start exploring one or two Southeast Asian markets in the coming quarters. The plans follow a $75 million injection of funds to go straight into the business by Kedaara Capital.

The company, which says it has grown about 30% a year for the past five years, is now earning double-digit EBITDA margins as a percentage of revenue, chief product officer Tom Welbury told Skift. 6 Airlines, 1 App: Why Lufthansa Group Wants To Be a Superbrand

Lufthansa Group is taking another step toward becoming a consumer brand in its own right with the launch of a new app that brings together six of its airlines under a single digital identity.

Unveiled on Monday, the app combines the digital services of Lufthansa, Swiss, Austrian Airlines, Brussels Airlines, ITA Airways, and Discover Airlines, alongside elements of the group’s Miles & More loyalty program. Passengers can book flights, purchase additional services, check in, access boarding passes, and track their baggage.

While much of the functionality will be familiar to users of the existing airline apps, Lufthansa Group chief commercial officer Dieter Vranckx described it as a logical step in developing the parent company’s brand and “making it more tangible” to passengers.

His comments this week echo an earlier observation that the firm “is evolving from a group of airlines into an integrated airline group.”

American Drops Lawsuit Over Gates at Chicago O’Hare but It’s Still Locked in a Battle With United

American Airlines dropped its lawsuit challenging Chicago’s 2025 decision to shift O’Hare International Airport gate space from American to United Airlines, days after losing an appeal in the case.

The reallocation, which took effect October 1, 2025, cost American more than 500 feet of gate space, about four narrow-body gates. American said it would operate out of seven fewer. United gained about four and a half.

American has since added three gates at O’Hare: two acquired from Spirit and one earned by growing at the airport.

item.title: 5 reasons to upgrade from the United Explorer to the United Quest
item.description:

Why it is here: clickbait, listicles and promotional

Quick summary

- A mid-tier airline card offers enhanced travel perks compared to a lower-tier option, including two free checked bags for the cardholder and a companion, annual airline credits and increased opportunities to earn elite status points.

- The higher-tier card provides automatic annual airline credits and more generous statement credits for ride-hailing, grocery delivery and hotel stays, which may offset its higher ongoing fee for frequent travelers.

- Both cards share core benefits such as priority boarding and credits for expedited airport security programs, but differ in the level and frequency of travel-related perks.

- Upgrading may be worthwhile for those who regularly check multiple bags, use airline credits or pursue elite status, while occasional travelers may find the lower-tier card sufficient.

What to consider

- To receive checked bag benefits, your loyalty program number must be included in the reservation and tickets must be purchased with the eligible card.

- Statement credits for services like ride-hailing and grocery delivery require activation and may have specific expiration dates or booking requirements.

- Upgrading does not typically provide a new cardholder bonus, so applying for a new account may be preferable if eligible.
